source.spoken_script: # The Two Goats — long-form narration (v1.2 — panel ×2, lock-ready) **Series:** types-shadows (#4) · **Format:** 16:9, ~6–8 min, 7-movement spine **Core text:** Leviticus 16 (the Day of Atonement) · **NT fulfillment (verbatim quotation):** Hebrews 9:12 · Hebrews 9:22 · Hebrews 10:4 · Hebrews 10:3 · Hebrews 10:11–12 · Hebrews 10:10 · Hebrews 10:19 · Hebrews 13:12 · Isaiah 53:6 · Matthew 27:51 · Psalm 103:12 **Thread (one spine, hook→landing — B-led, locked at /study):** One sin offering took **two** goats — because forgiveness has two halves: the price *paid* (the goat slain, its blood behind the veil) and the sin *carried away* (the live goat driven into the wilderness, never to return). One animal could not show both. The cross is the one act that did both — penalty paid and guilt removed — **once for all**, by the Priest who, when it was finished, **sat down**. Hook (why does one offering need two goats?) is paid off at the landing (your sin is not merely covered but carried away, "as far as the east is from the west"). **Status:** DRAFT v1.1 — thread LOCKED via `/study` (B-led: two goats = penalty paid + sin carried away; grafts the hands-on-the-head transfer, the year-by-year repetition / "this man sat down," and "without the gate" as movements). 1400 spoken words (LF-G5 PASS). All **18** KJV quotes self-checked verbatim against the cached corpus (Lev 16:2,5,8,10,15,21,22; Lev 17:11; Heb 9:12; 10:3,4,10,11,12,19; 13:12; Isa 53:6; Mt 27:51; Ps 103:12). **5-CLI panel DONE ×2 on clean artifacts.** Round 1 (`_independent_review/20260625-100915/`: claude PASS, cursor/codex/grok REVISE convergent; gemini env-failed) → applied all convergent fixes (below). **Round 2 unbiased re-panel** (`_independent_review/20260625-105323/`: cursor/claude/codex REVISE, gemini+grok env-failed; cursor confirmed "prior-panel issues appear fixed") → v1.2 convergent fixes: (A) **landing now names the gospel RESPONSE** — M7 "Your sin, if it is on Him… Come" (door opened, response unnamed) → "When sin is laid on Him… You have only to come — to trust the One who bore your sin… Come to Him, and be carried clean" (resolves the conditional + drops the universalizing "the sin is gone" before faith); (B) **M7 decoupled** the wilderness carry-away (Ps 103:12/scapegoat) from "outside the gate" (Heb 13:12/slain offering) — dropped "led outside the gate"; (C) **M4 "always taken"→"that day's offering"** (not all sin offerings went outside the camp); (D) **M5 "never the real thing"→"real, but never final"** + "not the final cure" (Lev 16:30's same-day cleansing was real); (E) **M6 "both goats"→"both halves… in a single death"** (no 1:1 NT claim; answers the live-goat-vs-crucified-Christ asymmetry); (F) **"torn by a hand from above"→"torn from above"** (no invented "hand"). DECLINED (advisory/locked-structure): restructure hook to lead with the goats (breaks 7-movement spine; hook rated strong by 2/3); ellipses on honest truncations (claude blessed); Heb 9:12 "holy places" plural (verified: standard KJV = "holy place" singular at 9:12; plural is 9:24 — cache matches standard). Round-1 convergent fixes were: (1) **M2 attribution** — "without shedding of blood is no remission" (Heb 9:22) was framed as "the Law's answer" → swapped to the Law's own blood-principle **Lev 17:11** "it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul"; (2) **M4 outside-the-camp** re-anchored to the **slain** offering's body burned outside the camp (Lev 16:27 / Heb 13:11), not the live scapegoat's wilderness route (dropped "where the sin-bearer always went"); (3) **removed the stacked debt/"bill"/"come due" accounting** (M4 "debt settled"→"borne in the sinner's place"; M5 "bill unpaid…come due"→"a cleansing they could not finally make…when does the true atonement come?"); (4) **qualified the OT-cleansing-was-real point** (M5 "actually"→"could finally take sin away"; M7 "not merely covered—waiting to surface"→"not merely covered for another year, the way it always was") so Lev 16:30's real

In Leviticus 16, one sin offering needs two goats, and only one of them dies.

The first goat is killed, its blood carried behind the veil. The second goat is never touched by a blade. The priest lays his hands on it, confesses the sin of the people, and sends it alive into the wilderness, never to return.

"Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering... and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat" - Leviticus 16:15

One goat pictures the price paid. The other pictures the guilt carried away. At the cross, one Priest did both, and sat down, because it was finished. Your sin is not just covered. It is carried away. Come to Him.

platforms.title: Why Did One Sacrifice Need Two Goats? (Leviticus 16 Explained)
platforms.description:
In Leviticus 16, on the Day of Atonement, the high priest does not sacrifice one goat. He needs two, and only one of them dies.

The first goat is killed, and its blood is carried behind the veil, into the Holy of Holies itself. The second goat is never touched by a blade. Aaron lays his hands on its head, confesses the sin of the people over it, and sends it alive into the wilderness, never to return (Leviticus 16:15-22).

Why two goats for one offering? Because forgiveness has two halves that no single animal could picture at once: the penalty that has to be paid, and the guilt that has to be carried away. One goat shows the price. The other shows the distance sin is removed to.

"Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the vail, and do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat:" - Leviticus 16:15

Every year, the priest does this again. The blood never finally finishes the job, until one Priest does both halves in a single death, and sits down, because the work is actually done (Hebrews 9:12; 10:10-12). What two goats needed a year to picture, the cross did once, for all.

If your sin is on Him, it is not just covered for another year. It is carried away, as far as the east is from the west. You have only to come.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- instagram description: "Your sin is not covered, it is carried away." drops the word "just" that every other platform keeps ("not just covered"). Read on its own this sentence sounds like it denies the goat's blood accomplished any covering at all, which contradicts Leviticus 16 itself and Hebrews 9:22 ("without shedding of blood is no remission") -- the thread's real point is that the OT covering was real but incomplete, not that it never covered anything. Fix: restore "just" -- "Your sin is not just covered. It is carried away."

- youtube_short slot: this entire kit is metadata for a 6-8 minute 16:9 LONG-FORM video (per the source facts), but a "youtube_short" title/description is generated anyway, describing this same long-form content as if it were a YouTube Short. No vertical short-form cut of this episode exists yet -- the project's own notes show Day of Atonement's 3 companion shorts are still unbuilt (zero narration text). Pasting this slot's copy against a ~10-minute 16:9 video would misrepresent the format to viewers expecting a <60s vertical clip. Fix: hold the youtube_short slot until a real short-form cut exists, or confirm with the user what asset it is meant to accompany before pasting it anywhere.

Everything else holds up under a hostile read: both KJV quotes (full and ellipsis-truncated) are exact verbatim substrings of the given anchor verse, no title overclaims or sensationalizes (all four candidates are true to Leviticus 16's actual two-goat structure), the "sat down" / Hebrews 9-10 framing matches the already-panel-locked narration's own resolved thread rather than inventing new doctrine, the landing CTA ("You have only to come") is grace-anchored with no fear or gain-loss pressure, and TikTok/Instagram lead with the same punchy hook line appropriate to short-attention platforms.
